author: marketing_c
protectedRevelations: Bounded verdicts on predictive claims and final research design

scenes.title: The chart feels personal
scenes.viewerPurpose: Recall a horoscope feeling strangely personal Expect a fair hearing followed by careful questions
scenes.composition: A reader recognizes themselves in a horoscope
addOrChange: Keep their reaction separate from the claim’s evidence, with no mystical control imagery.

cues.narration: A horoscope feels uncannily personal, but what exactly has recognized you?
cues.visualAction: Show the recognition, then the unresolved question beside it.

cues.narration: The Zodiac on Trial gives astrology a serious hearing before examining its claims.
cues.visualAction: Bring chart and evidence together without ridicule or endorsement.

scenes.title: The sky and the calendar
scenes.viewerPurpose: Separate observing seasons from predicting a life See several reasons a prediction might feel meaningful
scenes.composition: Seasonal timing and individual destiny remain different claims
addOrChange: Use one clear calendar cycle beside a separate personal chart.

cues.narration: It separates the sky as a calendar from the sky as an author of individual destiny.
cues.visualAction: Change the seasonal light while keeping the destiny claim separate.

cues.narration: Ancient sky watching, seasonal changes, and the feeling of being understood each get their turn.
cues.visualAction: Distinguish sky observation, seasonal conditions and personal recognition.

scenes.title: Recognition or prediction
scenes.viewerPurpose: Know both belief and skepticism must make a serious case Notice modern algorithms entering a familiar role
scenes.composition: A listener considers an astrological claim and a personalized algorithmic account
addOrChange: Replace mirror with two labeled descriptions and no truth badge.

cues.narration: Believers get a careful hearing, and skeptics are asked to answer their strongest arguments.
cues.visualAction: Give the strong claim and careful response equal attention.

cues.narration: The inquiry then turns toward algorithms that know far more about us.
cues.visualAction: The algorithmic description grows more detailed without proving its interpretation.

scenes.title: A fair hearing
scenes.viewerPurpose: Want patient inquiry rather than another easy joke Ask whether a feeling of truth proves its cause
scenes.composition: A personal reaction sits beside a declared test prediction
addOrChange: Simplify the protocol to one prediction and blank result.

cues.narration: If easy ridicule leaves you dissatisfied, this book offers a more patient investigation.
cues.visualAction: The reader opens the actual claim rather than a caricature.

cues.narration: When a description feels true, what would show that its explanation is true as well?
cues.visualAction: Hold prediction, blank result and recognition as distinct things.
